statement: A party in default shall not be entitled, without the leave of court, to raise any contest or dispute the claim of any other party to the action at the trial.
supporting_quote: Section 25(2) of Partition Law No.21 of 1977 reiterates that a party in default shall not be entitled, without the leave of court, raise any contest or dispute the claim of any other party to the action at the trial.

statement: The benefit of priority by registration accrues to a subsequent Deed for valuable consideration as against an earlier deed from the same source which is either not registered or not duly registered.
supporting_quote: It is settled law that the benefit of priority by registration accrues to a subsequent Deed for valuable consideration as against an earlier deed from the same source which is either not registered or not duly registered.

statement: A defendant who claims that the land sought to be partitioned is part of a larger land must follow the procedure laid down in section 19(2) of the Partition Law and move for the larger land to be partitioned.
supporting_quote: He cannot ask for dismissal of the action. Such a course of action is fair by all parties as it does not deprive the defendant of getting the larger land partitioned.

statement: A court can act only once and once only, and a succeeding judge cannot rescind the orders of a preceding judge.
supporting_quote: In the concept of functus officio, the personalities who make orders qua judicial officers do not matter. When the holder of the office has once discharged his duty, the duty has come to an end.

statement: A court can consider the reasonableness and legality of the basis on which a Competent Authority formed an opinion that a land is State land, when exercising its jurisdiction in terms of Article 140.
supporting_quote: This Court therefore takes the view that when exercising its jurisdiction in terms of Article 140, it is entitled to consider the reasonableness and the legality of the basis on which the Competent Authority formed his opinion as required by Section 3(1) of the Act.

statement: An interlocutory order in a Partition Act case is not a judgment, but an order with a final expression of the decision, and thus requires leave to appeal.
supporting_quote: It is to be noted that the question arises whether the Interlocutory Order of the learned Judge of the District Court of Ratnapura falls under Section 754(1) or 754(2) of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: An appeal does not lie against an order of dismissal made by the District Judge if the application, if decided in favour, would not have ended the case but would have proceeded with the trial and a fresh Judgment would have been delivered.
supporting_quote: When I adopt the Application Test to the present appeal, it is abundantly clear that, an appeal does not lie against the order of dismissal made by the District Judge. Notwithstanding the impugned order takes the shape of a final Judgment as it is, if the application of the 26th Defendant were to be decided in favour of her, the case would not have ended there, but the trial would have proceeded with, and a fresh Judgment would have been delivered.

statement: A prescriptive servitude of way must be precise and definite, relating to a defined track, and not consisting of proof of mere straying across an open land at any point which is at the moment most convenient.
supporting_quote: The evidence to establish a prescriptive servitude of way must be precise and definite. It must relate to a defined track, and must not consist of proof of mere straying across an open land at any point which is at the moment most convenient.

statement: A party cannot be inconsistent in their approach in legal proceedings, they cannot blow hot and cold, affirm and disaffirm the same transaction simultaneously to suit the occasion.
supporting_quote: He cannot blow hot and cold, affirm and disaffirm the same transaction simultaneously to suit the occasion.

statement: A person who claims prescriptive title against the rightful owner who has the paper title has a very heavy burden to prove all the requirements prescribed in section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: A person who claims prescriptive title against the rightful owner who has the paper title has a very heavy burden to prove all the requirements prescribed in section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.

statement: A party claiming prescriptive title must prove undisturbed and uninterrupted possession, independent or adverse to the claimant, for ten years prior to the action.
supporting_quote: In order to initiate a prescriptive title, it is necessary to show a change in the nature of the possession and the party claiming prescriptive right should show an ouster.

statement: A donation is not complete unless it is accepted by the donee.
supporting_quote: The general principle is that a donation is not complete unless it is accepted by the donee.

statement: A Court Commissioner's report can be used as evidence without further proof, subject to calling him as a witness, under section 18(2) of the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977, as amended.
supporting_quote: According to section 18(2) of the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977, as amended, that constitutes evidence without further proof subject to calling him, in terms of the proviso to section 18(2), as a witness.

statement: A person who bases their title in adverse possession must show by clear and unequivocal evidence that their possession was hostile to the real owner and amounted to a denial of their title to the property claimed.
supporting_quote: The principle of law is well established that a person who bases his title in adverse possession must show by clear and unequivocal evidence that his possession was hostile to the real owner and amounted to a denial of his title to the property claimed.

statement: A partition action can order that any portion of the land representing the share of any particular party only shall be demarcated and separated from the remainder of the land, and can also order that any share remain unallotted.
supporting_quote: In terms of section 26(2)(d) of the Partition Law, No. 21 of 1977, as amended, the District Judge, after trial inter alia can “order that any portion of the land representing the share of any particular party only shall be demarcated and separated from the remainder of the land”, and in terms of section 26(2)(g) can “order that any share remain unallotted”.

statement: A party claiming the benefit of Section 83 of the Trust Ordinance must establish that they did not intend to dispose of the beneficial interest in the property transferred.
supporting_quote: Where the owner of property transfers or bequeaths it, and it cannot reasonably be inferred consistently with the attendant circumstances that he intended to dispose of the beneficial interest therein, the transferee or legatee must hold such property for the benefit of the owner or his legal representative

statement: A co-owner cannot object to another co-owner possessing the common property.
supporting_quote: One co-owner cannot object to another co-owner possessing the common property.

statement: In a rei vindicatio action, the burden lies fairly and squarely on the plaintiff to prove his title to the land in the manner pleaded in the plaint.
supporting_quote: I must begin by stating that in a rei vindicatio action such as this, the burden lies fairly and squarely on the Plaintiff to prove his title to the land in the manner pleaded in the plaint.

statement: The pendency of civil proceedings does not constitute a legal bar to the institution or continuation of proceedings under Section 66.
supporting_quote: At its highest, the existence of such proceedings may be considered as surrounding circumstance, however, it does not undermine the Magistrate’s duty to inquire into the existence of a dispute affecting land and the likelihood of a breach of the peace, and to make such provisional orders as are necessary in that regard.

statement: A party does not need to establish a servitudanal right by cogent evidence as is usually considered in a civil Court. The required proof of the user's right in terms of Section 69 (1) of the Act, is to consider a right in the nature of a servitude or long terms use.
supporting_quote: In view of the Judgment Ananda Sarath Paranagama Vs. Dhammadinna Sarath Paranagama and Kamitha Aswin Paranagama CA (PHC) APN 117/2013, “A party does not need to establish a servitudanal right by cogent evidence as is usually considered in a civil Court. The required proof of the user’s right in terms of Section 69 (1) of the Act, is to consider a right in the nature of a servitude or long terms use”.

statement: A settlement in a partition case is not prohibited by the Partition Law if all parties with a right, share, or interest in the land have been made parties to the case and all of them participate in the settlement.
supporting_quote: Settlements in partition cases are not prohibited or obnoxious to the Partition Law provided (a) all the persons who have right, share or interest to, of, or in the land to be partitioned have been made parties to the case; and (b) all of them participate in the settlement.

statement: It is too late in the day to challenge the district court’s order on substitution both in law and facts.
supporting_quote: Hence the application of the substituted 01st defendant petitioner is dismissed with costs.

statement: A writ cannot lie if the disputed facts are within a contract or subject to private law and a specific remedy is available.
supporting_quote: What is here sought to be done is the enforcement of a Contract of employment, contracts of employment are enforceable by ordinary action and not by judicial review. In the circumstances the dispute as to the contract of employment is solely a matter within the purview of Private Law and not a matter for judicial review.

statement: State lands cannot be alienated on long lease without following the proper procedure; failure to do so is a violation of the Public Trust doctrine.
supporting_quote: State lands cannot be alienated on long lease without following the proper procedure; failure to do so is a violation of the Public Trust doctrine – vide Sugathapala Mendis v. Chandrika Kumaratunga [2008] 2 Sri LR 339 at 352.

statement: A decision to take immediate possession of land is ultra vires if the Minister of Lands fails to consider the necessity of taking over the land for the extension of the approach road.
supporting_quote: The Minister of Lands has failed to consider the necessity of taking over the land for the extension of the approach road;
